title: Torsion objects form a triangulated subcategory
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a pretriangulated category that is linear over a commutative ring $R$,
with $R$-linear shift functors, and let $M\subseteq R$ be a submonoid. The $M$-torsion
objects [def-sfb-torsion-objects] form a triangulated subcategory: they contain $0$, are
stable under shifts, and in a distinguished triangle
$X_1\to X_2\to X_3\to X_1[1]$, if $m_1$ kills $X_1$ and $m_3$ kills $X_3$, then
$m_1m_3$ kills $X_2$.

proof.text:
$1\cdot\mathrm{id}_0=0$. If $m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X=0$, then
$m\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X[n]}=(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X)[n]=0$, since the shift functors are linear.
For the triangle, write $u\colon X_1\to X_2$ and $v\colon X_2\to X_3$. Since
$v\circ(m_3\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_2})=(m_3\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_3})\circ v=0$, the long exact
sequence of $\Hom(X_2,-)$ gives $b\colon X_2\to X_1$ with
$m_3\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_2}=u\circ b$. Then
$$
(m_1m_3)\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_2}=m_1\cdot(u\circ b)=((m_1\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_2})\circ u)\circ b
=(u\circ(m_1\cdot\mathrm{id}_{X_1}))\circ b=0 .
$$
Since $M$ is a submonoid, $m_1m_3\in M$.

lean.note: The upstream instance exactly states that the M-torsion object property is a triangulated subcategory: it contains zero, is stable under all integer shifts, and is closed under distinguished triangles, with the product witness supplied by M.mul_mem. The companion declaration smul_id_obj₂_eq_zero gives the middle-object annihilation clause. Source: WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/DerivedCategory/Complete/Rationalization.lean.
